results.title: SUBSET PRODUCT instances

results.summary: An instance of SUBSET PRODUCT is a pair $(a, T)$ of a finite list $a$ of natural numbers and a target natural number $T$.

results.title: Well-formed SUBSET PRODUCT instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An instance $(a, T)$ of SUBSET PRODUCT, with $a$ a finite list of natural numbers and $T$ a natural number, is well formed when every entry of $a$ is positive.

results.title: Feasible SUBSET PRODUCT instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An instance $(a, T)$ of SUBSET PRODUCT, with $a$ a finite list of natural numbers and $T$ a natural number, is feasible when some sublist of $a$ (a list obtained from $a$ by deleting entries and keeping the order of the rest) has product exactly $T$.

results.title: SUBSET PRODUCT as a decision problem
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The decision problem SUBSET PRODUCT accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding of pairs of a finite list of natural numbers and a natural number, to an instance $(a, T)$ that is well formed (every entry of $a$ is positive) and feasible (some sublist of $a$ has product exactly $T$). It rejects every bitstring that does not decode to an instance.

results.title: SUBSET PRODUCT is NP-complete
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The decision problem SUBSET PRODUCT lies in NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to SUBSET PRODUCT.

results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ carry a relation $\le$. A Fibonacci tree with stored degree $d$, root $r \in \alpha$ and list of children $c$ is valid when every tree in $c$ is valid, $d$ equals the length of $c$, and $r \le x$ for every element $x$ of the multiset represented by the tree (the root together with the elements of all children).

results.title: One-element Fibonacci heap
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a value $x$ of a linearly ordered type, the one-element Fibonacci heap on $x$ has as its only tree the single-node tree with root $x$, and its cached minimum is $x$.

results.title: Linking two Fibonacci trees
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $s$ and $t$ be Fibonacci trees over a linearly ordered type. If the root of $s$ is at most the root of $t$, the link of $s$ and $t$ is the tree with the root of $s$, stored degree one more than that of $s$, and children $t$ followed by the children of $s$. Otherwise it is the tree with the root of $t$, stored degree one more than that of $t$, and children $s$ followed by the children of $t$.

results.title: Degree of the link of two trees of equal degree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If two Fibonacci trees $s$ and $t$ over a linearly ordered type have the same degree $d$, then their link has degree $d + 1$.

results.title: Linking adds the elements
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For any two Fibonacci trees $S$ and $T$ over a linearly ordered type, the tree obtained by linking $S$ and $T$ represents the sum of the multisets represented by $S$ and by $T$.

results.title: Singleton Fibonacci trees are valid
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type. For every $v \in \alpha$, the Fibonacci tree of degree $0$ with root $v$ and no children is valid.

results.title: Children of a valid Fibonacci tree are valid
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every child of a valid Fibonacci tree is itself a valid Fibonacci tree.

results.title: The degree of a valid Fibonacci tree is its number of children
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every valid Fibonacci tree, its stored degree equals the number of its children.

results.title: Roots of valid Fibonacci trees are lower bounds
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The root of a valid Fibonacci tree is no greater than every element of the multiset the tree represents.

results.title: The degree of a valid Fibonacci tree is less than its size
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every valid Fibonacci tree over a type with a relation $\le$, the degree of the tree is strictly less than the number of elements, counted with multiplicity, of the multiset the tree represents, since every child contributes at least one element.

results.title: Linking preserves validity of Fibonacci trees
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $s$ and $t$ are valid Fibonacci trees over a linearly ordered type, then the link of $s$ and $t$ is a valid Fibonacci tree.

results.title: Valid Fibonacci forests
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ carry a relation $\le$. A Fibonacci forest, a list of Fibonacci trees with values in $\alpha$, is valid when every tree in it is a valid Fibonacci tree.

results.title: Multiset of a Fibonacci forest
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Write $M(t)$ for the multiset of values stored in a Fibonacci tree $t$. The multiset represented by a Fibonacci forest, a list of Fibonacci trees $t_1, \dots, t_k$, is the sum $M(t_1) + \cdots + M(t_k)$; the empty forest represents the empty multiset.

results.title: Forests with strictly increasing degrees
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A Fibonacci forest, a list of Fibonacci trees $t_1, \dots, t_k$, has sorted degrees when the stored degrees of its trees strictly increase along the list: $\deg t_i < \deg t_j$ whenever $i < j$.

results.title: The empty Fibonacci forest is valid
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ carry a relation $\le$. The empty forest, containing no Fibonacci trees with values in $\alpha$, is valid.

results.title: Concatenation preserves validity of Fibonacci forests
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ carry a relation $\le$. If $F$ and $G$ are valid Fibonacci forests with values in $\alpha$, then the forest consisting of the trees of $F$ followed by the trees of $G$ is valid.

results.title: Sublists of valid Fibonacci forests are valid
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a list of Fibonacci trees is a valid forest, then every sublist of it (a subsequence, not necessarily contiguous) is a valid forest.

results.title: Elements of a concatenated forest
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For any two lists $L$ and $R$ of Fibonacci trees, the forest made of the trees of $L$ followed by the trees of $R$ represents the sum of the multisets represented by $L$ and by $R$.

results.title: Minimum root of a forest
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The minimum root of a forest of Fibonacci trees over a linearly ordered type is an optional value: it is absent for the empty forest, and for a nonempty forest it is the least of the roots of its trees.

results.title: Minimum of two optional values
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For optional values $x$ and $y$ of a linearly ordered type, their combined minimum is defined as follows: if $x$ and $y$ are both present, with values $a$ and $b$, it is $\min(a, b)$; if exactly one of $x$ and $y$ is present, it is that value; and if both are absent, it is absent.

results.title: Only the empty forest has no minimum root
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A forest of Fibonacci trees over a linearly ordered type has no minimum root exactly when it is empty.

results.title: The minimum root is a least root
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a forest $F$ of Fibonacci trees over a linearly ordered type has minimum root $m$, then $m$ is the root of some tree of $F$ and $m$ is at most the root of every tree of $F$.

results.title: Minimum root of a concatenated forest
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For forests $F$ and $G$ of Fibonacci trees over a linearly ordered type, the minimum root of $F$ followed by $G$ is the combined minimum of the optional minimum roots of $F$ and of $G$: their minimum if both exist, the one that exists if only one does, and absent if neither does.

results.title: Inserting a tree into a forest
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a Fibonacci tree $t$ and a list of Fibonacci trees, the insertion of $t$ into the list is defined recursively. Inserting $t$ into the empty list gives the one-tree list $[t]$. For a list with first tree $s$ and remaining list $L$: if the stored degree of $t$ is less than the stored degree of $s$, the result is $t$ followed by $s$ and then $L$; if the two stored degrees are equal, the result is the insertion…

results.title: Consolidation of a forest
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The consolidation of a list of Fibonacci trees is defined recursively: the consolidation of the empty list is the empty list, and the consolidation of a list with first tree $t$ and remaining list $L$ is the insertion of $t$ into the consolidation of $L$.

results.title: Consolidation preserves the elements
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list of Fibonacci trees over a linearly ordered type, its consolidation represents the same multiset as the original list.

results.title: Consolidation preserves validity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type. If a Fibonacci forest with values in $\alpha$ is valid, then its consolidation is valid.

results.title: Consolidation sorts root degrees
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list of Fibonacci trees, the stored degrees of the trees in its consolidation are strictly increasing in list order.

results.title: Consolidation yields distinct root degrees
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list of Fibonacci trees, the trees in its consolidation have pairwise distinct stored degrees.

results.title: Degree-sorted forests have at most as many trees as elements
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a valid forest of Fibonacci trees whose degrees are strictly increasing along the list. Then the number of trees in $F$ is at most the number of elements, counted with multiplicity, that $F$ represents.

results.title: Removing a minimum tree from a Fibonacci forest
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a list of Fibonacci trees over a linearly ordered type, this returns nothing on the empty list. Otherwise it returns the first tree whose root is minimal among all roots in the list, so earlier trees win ties, together with the list of the remaining trees in their original order.

results.title: Minimum-tree removal in a Fibonacci forest
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a list of Fibonacci trees over a linearly ordered type. If removing a minimum tree from $T$ returns a tree $m$ and a list $R$, then the multiset of elements of $m$ plus the multiset of elements of $R$ equals the multiset of elements of $T$, the tree $m$ belongs to $T$, the list $R$ is a sublist of $T$, and the root of $m$ is at most the root of every tree in $T$.

results.title: Fibonacci heap
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A Fibonacci min-heap over a linearly ordered type consists of a list of Fibonacci trees, each valid (heap-ordered, and at every node the stored degree equals the number of children), together with a cached minimum equal to the least root value of these trees, absent when the list is empty.

results.title: Multiset of a Fibonacci heap
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The multiset represented by a Fibonacci heap over a linearly ordered type is the multiset of its list of trees: the sum, over the trees in the list, of the multisets of values stored in them. The cached minimum plays no role.

results.title: Empty Fibonacci heap
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Fibonacci heap over a linearly ordered type whose list of trees is empty and whose cached minimum is absent.

results.title: Singleton Fibonacci heap
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a value $x$ of a linearly ordered type, the singleton Fibonacci heap on $x$ has as its only tree the single-node tree with root $x$, stored degree $0$ and no children, and its cached minimum is $x$.

results.title: Melding Fibonacci heaps
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The meld of Fibonacci heaps $H_1$ and $H_2$ is the Fibonacci heap whose root list is the root list of $H_1$ followed by that of $H_2$, and whose cached minimum is the smaller of the two cached minima when both heaps have one, and otherwise the cached minimum of whichever heap has one (none if neither does).

results.title: Union of Fibonacci heaps
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The union of Fibonacci heaps $H_1$ and $H_2$ is their meld: the heap whose trees are those of $H_1$ followed by those of $H_2$, and whose cached minimum is the smaller of the two cached minima (the one that exists if a heap is empty, none if both are).

results.title: Insertion into a Fibonacci heap
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Inserting a value $x$ into a Fibonacci heap $H$ gives the meld of the one-element Fibonacci heap containing $x$ with $H$, the one-element heap coming first.

results.title: Find-min for Fibonacci heaps
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Find-min on a Fibonacci heap returns its cached minimum without modifying the heap: the least root value of its trees, or no value when the heap has no trees.

results.title: Minimum deletion on a forest
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a list of Fibonacci trees over a linearly ordered type, the result is nothing if the list is empty. Otherwise the first tree whose root is minimal is removed, and the result is its root value together with the consolidation of the forest made of the removed tree's children followed by the remaining trees.

results.title: Deleting the minimum of a Fibonacci heap
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: If the root list of the heap is empty, the result is nothing. Otherwise the first tree of the root list whose root is minimal is removed, and the result is its root value together with the heap whose root list is the consolidation of the removed tree's children followed by the remaining trees, and whose cached minimum is the minimum root of this consolidated forest.

results.title: Fibonacci heap minimum deletion agrees with its root-list version
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every Fibonacci heap $H$, deleting the minimum of $H$ and keeping only the returned value and the root list of the resulting heap gives the same result as the root-list minimum deletion applied to the root list of $H$: either both fail, or both return the same value and the same list of trees.

results.title: The empty Fibonacci heap has no elements
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The empty Fibonacci heap represents the empty multiset.

results.title: Multiset of a singleton Fibonacci heap
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every value $x$ of a linearly ordered type, the singleton Fibonacci heap on $x$, whose only tree is the single-node tree with root $x$, represents the multiset $\{x\}$.

results.title: Melding adds the elements
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For any two Fibonacci heaps $H_1$ and $H_2$ over a linearly ordered type, the meld of $H_1$ and $H_2$ represents the sum of the multisets represented by $H_1$ and by $H_2$.

results.title: The union of Fibonacci heaps adds their multisets
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For Fibonacci heaps $H_1$ and $H_2$ over a linearly ordered type, the multiset represented by the union of $H_1$ and $H_2$ is the sum of the multisets represented by $H_1$ and by $H_2$.

results.title: Insertion adds one occurrence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every Fibonacci heap $H$ over a linearly ordered type and every value $x$, the heap obtained by inserting $x$ into $H$ represents the multiset of $H$ with one more occurrence of $x$.

results.title: Melding adds the sizes of Fibonacci heaps
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For Fibonacci heaps $H_1$ and $H_2$, the number of elements of the meld of $H_1$ and $H_2$, counted with multiplicity, is the number of elements of $H_1$ plus the number of elements of $H_2$.

results.title: Insertion increases the size of a Fibonacci heap by one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every Fibonacci heap $H$ and every value $x$, the number of elements of the heap obtained by inserting $x$ into $H$, counted with multiplicity, is the number of elements of $H$ plus one.

results.title: Find-min fails exactly on the empty Fibonacci heap
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a Fibonacci heap $H$ over a linearly ordered type, find-min on $H$ returns no value if and only if $H$ has no trees.

results.title: Find-min returns an element of the Fibonacci heap
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $H$ be a Fibonacci heap over a linearly ordered type. If find-min on $H$ returns $m$, then $m$ belongs to the multiset represented by $H$.

results.title: Find-min returns a lower bound of the Fibonacci heap
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $H$ be a Fibonacci heap over a linearly ordered type. If find-min on $H$ returns $m$, then $m \le v$ for every value $v$ in the multiset represented by $H$.

results.title: Fibonacci heap minimum deletion fails exactly on the empty heap
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Deleting the minimum of a Fibonacci heap fails if and only if the heap's list of root trees is empty.

results.title: Fibonacci heap minimum deletion removes one copy of the minimum
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If deleting the minimum of a Fibonacci heap $H$ succeeds and returns the value $m$ and the heap $H'$, then the multiset of elements of $H'$ is the multiset of elements of $H$ with one occurrence of $m$ removed.

results.title: Fibonacci heap minimum deletion splits off the minimum
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If deleting the minimum of a Fibonacci heap $H$ succeeds and returns the value $m$ and the heap $H'$, then the multiset of elements of $H$ is the multiset of elements of $H'$ with one copy of $m$ added.

results.title: Fibonacci heap minimum deletion returns a lower bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If deleting the minimum of a Fibonacci heap $H$ succeeds and returns the value $m$, then $m \le v$ for every element $v$ of $H$.

results.title: Minimum deletion leaves a Fibonacci heap with strictly increasing root degrees
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If deleting the minimum of a Fibonacci heap succeeds and returns the heap $H'$, then the degrees of the root trees of $H'$, in list order, are strictly increasing; consolidation is what makes them so.

results.title: After minimum deletion a Fibonacci heap has at most as many roots as elements
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If deleting the minimum of a Fibonacci heap succeeds and returns the heap $H'$, then the number of root trees of $H'$ is at most the number of elements of $H'$, counted with multiplicity.

results.title: Subtree of a Fibonacci tree at a path
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a list $p = (i_1, \dots, i_n)$ of natural numbers and a Fibonacci tree $t$, the subtree of $t$ at $p$ is found by starting at the root and moving to the child with zero-based index $i_1$, then to its child with index $i_2$, and so on. The result is absent when some index is at least the number of children of the current node. The empty path addresses the whole tree $t$.

results.title: Cutting a subtree out of a Fibonacci tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a path $p$ of child indices and a Fibonacci tree $t$, the cut of $t$ at $p$ is either undefined or a pair of an extracted subtree and an optional remainder tree. For the empty path, the extracted subtree is $t$ and there is no remainder. For a path consisting of an index $i$ followed by a path $q$, where $t$ has root $r$ and children $c_0, \dots, c_{k-1}$, the cut is undefined if $i \ge k$ or if the cut of…

results.title: Replacing the root key of a Fibonacci tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a Fibonacci tree $t$ and a key $k$, this is the tree whose root value is $k$ and whose stored degree and list of children are those of $t$.

results.title: Elements after replacing the root key
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a Fibonacci tree $t$ and any key $k$, the multiset of elements represented by the tree obtained from $t$ by replacing its root value with $k$ equals the multiset of elements of $t$ with one occurrence of the root of $t$ removed and $k$ added.

results.title: Lowering the root keeps a Fibonacci tree valid
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a valid Fibonacci tree over a preordered type and let $k$ be a key that is at most the root of $T$. Then the tree obtained from $T$ by replacing its root by $k$, keeping its degree and children, is valid: the new root is still no greater than every represented element.

results.title: Subtrees of a valid Fibonacci tree are valid
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a Fibonacci tree $t$ is valid and a path $p$ of child indices addresses a subtree $s$ of $t$, then $s$ is valid.

results.title: A cut extracts the addressed subtree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$ be a Fibonacci tree and $p$ a path of child indices. If cutting $t$ at $p$ extracts a subtree $s$ (with or without a remainder), then $s$ is the subtree of $t$ at $p$.

results.title: Every addressed subtree can be cut out
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a path $p$ of child indices addresses a subtree $s$ of a Fibonacci tree $t$, then cutting $t$ at $p$ succeeds and extracts exactly $s$, together with some remainder, which may be absent.

results.title: A cut without remainder extracts the whole tree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$ be a Fibonacci tree and $p$ a path of child indices. If cutting $t$ at $p$ extracts a subtree $s$ and leaves no remainder, then $s = t$.

results.title: Cutting a subtree splits the elements of a Fibonacci tree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$ be a Fibonacci tree and $p$ a path of child indices. If cutting $t$ at $p$ extracts a subtree $s$ and leaves a remainder tree $t'$, then the multiset of elements of $t$ is the sum of the multisets of elements of $t'$ and of $s$.

results.title: The subtree extracted by a cut from a valid tree is valid
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$ be a valid Fibonacci tree over a type with a relation $\le$, and $p$ a path of child indices. If cutting $t$ at $p$ extracts a subtree $s$ (with or without a remainder), then $s$ is valid.

results.title: The remainder of a cut from a valid tree is valid
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$ be a valid Fibonacci tree over a type with a relation $\le$, and $p$ a path of child indices. If cutting $t$ at $p$ extracts a subtree and leaves a remainder tree $t'$, then $t'$ is valid: its children are valid, its stored degree equals its number of children, and its root is $\le$ every element of $t'$.

results.title: Cutting a subtree out of a Fibonacci forest
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a forest given as a list of Fibonacci trees, an index $i$ and a path $p$ of child indices, the cut is undefined if the list has no tree at position $i$ (counting from $0$) or if cutting that tree $t$ at $p$ is undefined. Otherwise, if cutting $t$ at $p$ extracts the subtree $s$, the result is $s$ together with the list in which the tree at position $i$ is removed (if the cut of $t$ left no remainder) or…

results.title: Cutting a subtree splits the elements of a Fibonacci forest
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a forest of Fibonacci trees, $i$ an index and $p$ a path of child indices. If cutting $F$ at the $i$-th tree and path $p$ extracts a subtree $s$ and leaves the forest $F'$, then the multiset of elements of $F$ is the sum of the multisets of elements of $F'$ and of $s$.

results.title: Cutting a valid forest leaves valid parts
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a valid forest of Fibonacci trees over a type with a relation $\le$, $i$ an index and $p$ a path of child indices. If cutting $F$ at index $i$ and path $p$ extracts a subtree $s$ and leaves the forest $F'$, then $s$ is a valid tree and $F'$ is a valid forest.

results.title: Every addressed subtree of a forest can be cut out
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a forest of Fibonacci trees whose tree at position $i$ is $t$, and let $p$ be a path of child indices such that the subtree of $t$ at $p$ is $s$. Then cutting $F$ at index $i$ and path $p$ is defined and extracts $s$, together with some remaining forest.

results.summary: Let $H$ be a Fibonacci heap, $i$ a root index, $p$ a path of child indices and $k$ a key. Suppose that cutting the subtree at path $p$ out of the $i$-th tree of the root list of $H$ succeeds, extracting the subtree $S$ and leaving the forest $R$, and that $k$ is at most the root of $S$. results.title: Decrease-key at an unresolved address does nothing
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $H$ be a Fibonacci heap, $i$ a root index and $p$ a path of child indices. If cutting the subtree at path $p$ out of the $i$-th tree of the root list of $H$ fails, then for every key $k$, decreasing the key at root index $i$ and path $p$ to $k$ returns $H$ unchanged.

results.title: Decrease-key with a larger key does nothing
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $H$ be a Fibonacci heap, $i$ a root index, $p$ a path of child indices and $k$ a key. Suppose that cutting the subtree at path $p$ out of the $i$-th tree of the root list of $H$ succeeds and extracts the subtree $S$, and that $k$ is not at most the root of $S$ (keys are linearly ordered, so $k$ is greater than that root). Then decreasing the key at root index $i$ and path $p$ to $k$ returns $H$ unchanged.

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $H$ be a Fibonacci heap, $i$ a root index, $p$ a path of child indices and $k$ a key. Suppose that cutting the subtree at path $p$ out of the $i$-th tree of the root list of $H$ succeeds and extracts the subtree $S$, and that $k$ is at most the root of $S$. Then the multiset represented by the heap obtained from $H$ by decreasing the key at root index $i$ and path $p$ to $k$ is the multiset represented by $H$…

results.title: Decrease-key replaces one key, stated by address
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $H$ be a Fibonacci heap, let $T$ be the $i$-th tree of its root list, and let $S$ be the subtree of $T$ at the path $p$ of child indices. If the key $k$ is at most the root of $S$, then the multiset represented by the heap obtained from $H$ by decreasing the key at root index $i$ and path $p$ to $k$ is the multiset represented by $H$ with one occurrence of the root of $S$ removed and one occurrence of $k$ added.

results.title: Decrease-key preserves the number of elements
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $H$ be a Fibonacci heap, $i$ a root index, $p$ a path of child indices and $k$ a key. Suppose that cutting the subtree at path $p$ out of the $i$-th tree of the root list of $H$ succeeds and extracts the subtree $S$, and that $k$ is at most the root of $S$. Then the multiset represented by the heap obtained from $H$ by decreasing the key at root index $i$ and path $p$ to $k$ has the same number of elements,…

Suppose that cutting the subtree at path $p$ out of the $i$-th tree of the root list of $H$ succeeds and extracts the subtree $S$, and that $k$ is at most the root of $S$. results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every Fibonacci heap $H$, root index $i$, path $p$ of child indices and key $k$, the root list of the heap obtained from $H$ by decreasing the key at root index $i$ and path $p$ to $k$ is a valid forest, that is, every tree in it is valid.

results.title: Entries of the min-plus matrix accumulator

results.title: Correctness of the string-matching transition table
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $P$ be a pattern of length $m$ over the alphabet $\{0, \dots, A-1\}$ and write $P_k$ for its prefix of length $k$. results.title: Cost bound for the string-matching transition table

results.title: String-matching automaton

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $a \ge b \ge c \ge d \ge e$ be natural numbers. The Princess and the Roses position $(a, b, c, d, e)$ is a P-position if and only if the parities of $a, b, c, d, e$ are, in this order, (even, even, even, even, even), (odd, odd, odd, even, even), (even, odd, odd, odd, odd) or (odd, even, even, odd, odd).

results.title: Sprague–Grundy values of two-pile Princess and the Roses
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $a \ge b$, the Princess and the Roses position $(a, b)$ is equivalent to the Nim heap $*n$, that is, it has Sprague–Grundy value $n$, where $n = 0$ if $a$ and $b$ are both even, $n = 1$ if $a$ is odd and $b$ is even, $n = 2$ if $a$ and $b$ are both odd, and $n = 3$ if $a$ is even and $b$ is odd.

results.title: P&R Helper positions of Sprague–Grundy value 6 or 7 on region U
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $x \le y \le z$ with $z < x + y$ and $y \le 2x + 1$ (the region $U$), the P&R Helper game started at $[x, y, z]$ is equivalent to the Nim heap of size $6$ (that is, has Sprague–Grundy value $6$) if and only if $y = x + 2$, $z = x + 5$ and $x \equiv 1 \pmod 8$; and it is never equivalent to the Nim heap of size $7$.

results.summary: Let $x \le y \le z$ be natural numbers with $z < x + y$ and $y > 2x + 1$ (the region $R$), and write $s = y + z - x$. For every natural number $n$, the P&R Helper game started at $[x, y, z]$ is equivalent to the Nim heap of size $n$ (that is, has Sprague–Grundy value $n$) if and only if one of the following holds: $n = 0$ and $x$, $y$, $z$ are all even; $n = 1$ and $s \equiv 1 \pmod 4$; $n = 2$, $x$ is even and…

results.title: Sprague–Grundy values of P&R Helper on region L
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $x \le y \le z$ be natural numbers with $z \ge x + y$ and $y \le 2x$ (the region $L$). For every natural number $n$, the P&R Helper game started at $[x, y, z]$ is equivalent to the Nim heap of size $n$ (that is, has Sprague–Grundy value $n$) if and only if one of the following holds: $n = 0$ and $x$, $y$, $z$ are all even; $n = 1$, $x$ and $y$ are even and $z$ is odd; $n = 2$ and $y + 2z - 2x \equiv 3 \pmod 4$;…
